summary: BLM lookout cabin on East Butte, Bingham County; Ralph King and his wife were known personnel in 1961; duties moved to Big Southern Butte; site now gone.

facts.status_note: firelookout.com lists the East Butte lookout as gone, with no date. Wikipedia says the summit now has radio towers.

access.note: The summit is on Idaho National Laboratory land. Wikipedia says access is restricted, though a road leads to radio towers at the top.

visit.trail_note: No lookout is described as standing. Access is restricted per Wikipedia; no public visit is described.

events.note: firelookout.com lists Mr. & Mrs. Ralph King as known lookout personnel for 1961.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict, unresolved: Wikipedia gives 6,572 ft for the summit, firelookout.com gives 6,549 ft for the lookout site, and the 1962 article gives 6,800 ft for the butte with the lookout 1,010 ft above it. Build date unknown: firelookout.com lists a cabin from the 1950s with a question mark. The 1961 staffing entry is from firelookout.com; the 1962 article's 'last summer' is consistent with it but names no year. The removal date and cause are not in any source read. Name variant 'Little Butte' comes from the Forest Lookouts page header. Do not confuse with the East Butte Lookout in Deschutes County, Oregon (nhlr cache: data/raw/nhlr/nhlr.org/lookouts/us/or/east-butte-lookout). No new photo added.
